_comment: Model endpoints and prices. Verify prices against https://fal.ai/pricing before a rung-3 run; fal changes them without notice.
_pricing_version_note: Bump this integer any time a rate, markup, or pricing rule below actually changes. webapp/server.py's quote endpoints echo it back; the generate endpoints check it against a client-supplied pricing_version (when present) the same way they already check approved_cost -- a stale quote from before a bump is rejected with a clear 're-quote' error instead of silently running at whatever this process's current rate happens to be. Since CONFIG is loaded once per process (see factory.load_config()), this mainly guards a browser tab left open across a redeploy, not a live race within one process's lifetime.

pricing._note: Applied ONLY in webapp/server.py, to every customer-facing price: quotes, the confirm dialog, credit-balance charges, and (since mcp/server.py talks to the webapp's own API rather than reading this file) MCP tool output too. scripts/factory.py's CLI always shows the real wholesale fal.ai rate unchanged -- it's the operator's own tool against their own fal.ai balance, not a customer-facing surface, so there's nothing to mark up there. work/generations.jsonl (the internal spend ledger) always logs both numbers -- cost_usd stays the real wholesale spend (unchanged meaning from before this existed), customer_charged_usd is what was actually billed -- so margin is visible internally without touching this file. 1.12 (a 12% margin) is a deliberately thin, growth-stage price -- picked so the product can compete on price against Higgsfield/Montage.ai while the user base is small, not to maximize margin per video yet. Change this one number to change profit margin; nothing else needs editing.

_model_choice_note: Per-shot model routing lives in fal-master-prompt.md section 5. Short version: Kling 3.0 Standard is the default (cheapest proven option, matches this user's own Higgsfield clips, strong action/motion/lip-sync). LTX-2.3 for cost-sensitive or long single-take shots (verified cheapest at $0.06/s 1080p, up to 20s in one call, vertical-native -- untested on this project's actual likeness-holding yet, so not a blind default). Veo 3.1 for face-critical calm/dialogue close-ups. Seedance 2.0 for a hero shot with heavy physics/particle simulation that justifies its price. Seedance 2.5 and FLUX 3 are the two 'top quality, cost no object' options -- both meaningfully more expensive than everything else here, offered as an explicit opt-in tier for a user who has said price isn't the deciding factor, never chosen automatically. See each rate's own _note for the caveats that come with picking them.

final_take_per_second_usd_by_model._note: Keyed by exact fal model id, not a nickname. cmd_cost/cmd_final refuse to run for a --model not listed here, rather than guess a price -- add the real per-second rate first (check fal.ai/pricing). LTX-2.3's 0.06 is the 1080p tier; 1440p is 0.12 and 4K is 0.24 -- add those as separate model ids (e.g. with a resolution suffix) if a shot needs them, don't silently reuse this rate at a different resolution. FLUX 3's 0.17 is its 720p tier; 1080p is 0.29/s and, same as LTX, needs a separate model id if wired -- not done here since this project defaults final takes to 1080p elsewhere but FLUX 3 isn't the default for anything, so the cheaper tier is what a caller opting into it explicitly gets quoted. Seedance 2.5 is priced DIFFERENTLY from every other row here: fal bills it by a token formula (output width x height x duration x 24 / 1024, at $0.0214/1000 tokens), not a flat per-second rate, and fal's own docs confirm 'wider aspect ratios ... cost more per second, narrower ones cost less' -- 0.4730 is the confirmed approximation for standard 16:9 only. cmd_final refuses to quote/run this model unless the actual start-frame image is 16:9 (checked via ffprobe), specifically so this approximation can never silently under- or over-charge against what --i-approve-cost approved. Hailuo-02's 0.045 is its 768P tier (512P is 0.017, a separate 1080p 'Pro' endpoint is ~0.08 -- not wired, same rule as LTX/FLUX3's other tiers). PixVerse v6's pricing varies by BOTH resolution and an audio on/off switch (4 resolutions x 2 audio states); 0.060 is the 720p-with-audio price, matching this project's own default resolution and final_audio=true -- picking a different resolution through this model isn't exposed, since doing so would silently misprice against this flat rate the same way Seedance 2.5's aspect-ratio caveat works, and no ffprobe-style check exists for resolution the way one does for aspect ratio.

upscale_per_second_usd_by_tier._note: fal-ai/topaz/upscale/video, keyed by OUTPUT resolution tier (not input) -- confirmed from that model's own pricing panel on fal.ai. cmd_upscale doubles this automatically for --fps 60+. Some Topaz model variants (e.g. a 'Gaia 2' one) reportedly bill about half this on fal's panel, but the exact enum spelling wasn't confirmed against the live schema so that discount isn't auto-applied -- treat the quoted number as an upper bound if you pick a Gaia-family --model.

rates._post_production_note: lipsync_per_second_usd ($8/min = ~$0.1333/s) and bg_remove_per_second_usd ($0.0042/s) are both confirmed directly on their model's own fal.ai page ('Your request will cost $X per second'). transcription_per_second_usd is NOT confirmed on fal-ai/wizper's docs page (checked; not shown there) -- it's a conservative estimate from third-party aggregator data on fal's Whisper-family pricing. Verify it against your fal.ai dashboard invoice after the first real subtitles run and correct this number if it's off; the absolute cost is small regardless (a few cents for a whole film's dialogue).
rates._motion_transfer_note: fal-ai/kling-video/v2.6/standard/motion-control's own pricing panel confirms 'Your request will cost $0.07 per second' -- billed by the SOURCE video's duration (probed via ffprobe, same as lipsync/avatar), not the output. This is the cost-effective 'standard' tier (good for portraits/simple animations, character_orientation='video' matches the reference video's framing, max ~30s); the pricier v3/pro tier (complex choreography) isn't wired here -- add it as a second model id the same way final_take's alt models work if that quality level is ever needed.

defaults.negative_prompt: slow motion unless explicitly requested, morphing, warping, melting, flickering, frame stutter, unnatural physics, ragdoll glitches, extra limbs, distorted or drifting face, identity change, low detail, compression artifacts, motion smear on the face

polish._note: Free, local, ffmpeg-only -- no fal cost. Mild filmic S-curve + vignette + fine grain. smooth_fps doubles 24fps source via motion-compensated interpolation when --smooth is passed. --deflicker (also free/local) is a separate flag, not folded into this filter chain.

subtitles._note: DejaVu Sans is confirmed to render Cyrillic correctly -- verified during the '25 yil' film's manual drawtext burn-in. Keep this font unless a replacement is verified the same way (missing glyphs render as boxes, easy to miss in a quick preview).
